It took 8 years to conquer Spain.

It took 770 years to take it back.

The Reconquista, the longest war in European history — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ 711: Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses from Morocco. Within a decade, the Visigothic kingdom is gone and Muslim armies stand at the Pyrenees.

All that holds out is the map's thin dark sliver in the northern mountains — where legend says Pelayo won at Covadonga, ~722.

2/ For 300 years the line barely moves — look how close together the 750, 800 and 1045 bands sit.

Meanwhile al-Andalus becomes Europe's richest society: Córdoba has street lighting, libraries of 100,000+ books, and scholars translating the Greeks while Paris is a muddy town.

3/ The breakthrough: Toledo falls in 1085. Then, in 1212, the combined kings of Castile, Aragón and Navarra crush the Almohads at Las Navas de Tolosa.

After that, the dam breaks: Córdoba 1236, Valencia 1238, Seville 1248 — the huge 1270 band swallows half the peninsula.

4/ Then... nothing, for 250 years.

Granada — the map's small 1492 strip — survives as a tributary, paying gold to Castile and building the Alhambra.

It lives by playing Christian kingdoms against each other until Ferdinand and Isabella unite them by marriage.

5/ January 2, 1492: Boabdil hands over the keys of Granada.

The same year, the same monarchs expel Spain's Jews and fund a Genoese sailor named Columbus.

The energy and machinery of the Reconquista rolls straight into the conquest of the Americas.

6/ The 770-year war left Spanish full of Arabic — azúcar, aceite, ojalá — and left Iberia with a crusading state machine that would conquer half the world.
